title: An equivalence of categories induces an equivalence of homological-complex categories
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category] with zero morphisms, let $e:\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal D$ be an equivalence whose forward functor preserves zero morphisms, and let $c$ be a complex shape. Applying the forward and inverse functors termwise gives an equivalence $\operatorname{HomologicalComplex}(\mathcal C,c)\simeq\operatorname{HomologicalComplex}(\mathcal D,c)$. Its unit and counit are the natural isomorphisms obtained degreewise from the unit and counit of $e$, and they satisfy the triangle identities. Here zero morphisms are chosen maps $0_{U,V}$ annihilated by composition on either side. A functor preserves identities and composition; a natural transformation has components commuting with every morphism, and a natural isomorphism has invertible components. The equivalence $e$ consists of functors $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ and natural isomorphisms $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to GF$, $\varepsilon:FG\to\mathrm{id}$ satisfying $\varepsilon_{FX}F(\eta_X)=\mathrm{id}$ and $G(\varepsilon_Y)\eta_{GY}=\mathrm{id}$. A complex shape on an index set $I$ is a relation $c(i,j)$ having at most one successor and one predecessor at each index. A complex of this shape has objects $K_i$, maps $d_{ij}:K_i\to K_j$ with $d_{ij}=0$ unless $c(i,j)$, and $d_{jk}d_{ij}=0$; its morphisms are families commuting with the differentials. These form $\operatorname{HomologicalComplex}(\mathcal C,c)$. The same definition applies to $\mathcal D$.
